style: Say in a relaxed, friendly way, like a parent who packs lunches and loves a kitchen experiment.
lines: Lunch rides in a hot car from eight until noon. Tap a material to add a wall layer, then tap Run.
Three layers is the limit. Tap a layer in the box to take it out.
Take out a pack first. Thicker walls leave less room inside.
No room for another pack. Thicker walls leave less room inside.
Watch the red lunch line. In this model, lunch stays cold in the blue zone.
See the flat blue line at zero? The ice is melting. Melting takes in heat without getting warmer.
You changed the box, so the test starts over at eight. Tap Run when you're ready.
Cold until noon. Job done.
Cold until noon, but it's over budget. Can you do it for eight dollars?
Lunch left the cold zone early. Change one thing and run it again.
Two quick questions from the engineer. Tap one answer for each.
Right.
Not quite. Read why.
Last step: in the note box, say which change helped most. Your log is the evidence.
In the note box, explain how one part helped your design. Use your test as evidence.
Welcome to the test bench. Tap a question, then set A and B so only one thing is different.
Fair test.
Not a fair test yet. Read the note, fix it, and tap Check plan.
Predict: tap A, B or Same, then Run.
Both samples get the same heat. Watch how far each line moves.
The samples get different amounts of heat. Watch how far each line moves.
Tap the sentence your graph supports. You get one try.
Three tests complete. All three first claims supported by your graphs.
Three tests complete. Some claims need review. Compare the corrections with your graphs.
Lunch rides in a hot car from 8:00 to noon. Tap a material to add a wall layer, or tap Run to test the bare box.
Tap a material or a pack to add it. Tap a layer label or a pack in the box to remove it. Tap Run to test.
Tap a question first.
Set A and B so only your question’s variable differs. Then tap Check plan.
Note saved on this device.
A and B are the same. Change the one thing your question is about.
Keep lunch at four degrees Celsius or colder until noon. Budget eight dollars. Walls at most thirty millimeters. Pack at least two cold sources.
Watch the lunch line. Tap Skip to noon to finish, or change a part to restart.
Ice is melting at zero without warming. Tap Skip to noon, or change a part to restart.
The ice has melted; its line rises again. Watch lunch, or tap Skip to noon.
Prediction set. Tap Run to test your plan.
